_README: Human meaning for the published contract API. Build input, not an artefact.
scripts/build-contract-api.mjs extracts WHICH finding codes exist, with what
severity and from which function, by loading the published runtime bytes. It
cannot extract what a code MEANS, what an author should do about it, or whether
a conformance requirement is decidable by a tool. That is what this file holds.
The gate refuses a mismatch in BOTH directions: a code the runtime emits with no
entry here, and an entry here for a code the runtime no longer emits. Level
requirements are keyed by the sha384 of their text in SPEC.md section 8, so
editing the sentence turns the gate red until someone re-reads the mapping.
A published conformance level that nobody re-read is how a guarantee rots.

manifest_role_unknown.what: A manifest element declares a data-nac-role that is not in the runtime's accepted role set.
manifest_role_unknown.fix: Use one of the roles published in contract.json, or drop the role and let the element default to action behaviour.

tab_id_manifest_role_drift.what: An id matching the reserved tab. prefix carries a role other than tab, so NAC.tab() and NAC.tab_by_label() will never resolve it.
tab_id_manifest_role_drift.fix: Set role to tab, or rename the id out of the reserved tab. prefix.

manifest_dom_role_mismatch.what: The manifest and the mounted DOM element disagree about the role of the same id.
manifest_dom_role_mismatch.fix: Make the data-nac-role attribute on the element match the role declared in the manifest.

duplicate_plugin_no_instance_id.what: The same plugin slug is mounted more than once and the instances carry no distinct data-nac-plugin-id, so no id under that slug resolves to one element.
duplicate_plugin_no_instance_id.fix: Give every mounted instance a unique data-nac-plugin-id, or mount the plugin once.

no_manifest.what: Validation was asked for a plugin slug that was never registered.
no_manifest.fix: Call NAC.register() for that slug before validating it, or correct the slug.

plugin_not_mounted.what: The plugin is registered but no element with its data-nac-plugin root is in the DOM.
plugin_not_mounted.fix: Mount the plugin root before validating, or unregister it when the view unmounts.

missing_in_dom.what: An id the manifest advertises has no element in the DOM, so an agent that trusts the manifest will fail to operate it.
missing_in_dom.fix: Render the element, or remove the id from the manifest while it is not mounted.

field_type_mismatch.what: The manifest declares a field type the mounted element contradicts.
field_type_mismatch.fix: Align the manifest type with data-nac-field-type on the element.

field_type_undeclared.what: A field is advertised without a type, so an agent has to guess how to fill it.
field_type_undeclared.fix: Declare the field type in the manifest.

options_unresolved.what: A field advertises options and no resolver or option element produces them.
options_unresolved.fix: Provide the options resolver, or mark the field as free text.

depends_on_orphan.what: A manifest entry depends on an id that nothing in the manifest declares.
depends_on_orphan.fix: Declare the referenced id, or remove the dependency.

row_cell_missing.what: A data table declares a column with no matching cell in a row, so cell addressing by column breaks.
row_cell_missing.fix: Render every declared column in every row, or drop the column declaration.

breadcrumb_item_missing.what: A declared breadcrumb hop has no matching breadcrumb-item element in the DOM.
breadcrumb_item_missing.fix: Render the breadcrumb item, or remove the hop from the manifest.

duplicate_tab_label.what: Two tabs under one plugin share a label, so NAC.tab_by_label() is ambiguous.
duplicate_tab_label.fix: Make the labels distinct, or address those tabs by id only.

duplicate_verb.what: Two actions under one plugin declare the same data-nac-action verb, so NAC.click_by_verb() cannot resolve it. SPEC.md section 3 names this a manifest error.
duplicate_verb.fix: Make the verb unique within the plugin, or address those actions by id.

aria_nac_state_mismatch.what: The ARIA state of an element and its data-nac-state disagree, so a screen reader and an agent see different truths about the same widget.
aria_nac_state_mismatch.fix: Mirror the two: update data-nac-state wherever the ARIA attribute changes.

drag_type_unknown.what: A drag type or accept value falls outside the registry. Custom types still work; this is a heads-up that no agent can guess the semantics.
drag_type_unknown.fix: Use a registered drag type, or document the custom one for the agents that must handle it.

skip_without_reason.what: A subtree is excluded from validation with no reason recorded, so the exclusion cannot be reviewed.
skip_without_reason.fix: State the reason on the skip annotation.

skip_no_remediate_date.what: A validation exclusion carries no remediation date, so it has no expiry and becomes permanent debt.
skip_no_remediate_date.fix: Add the date by which the exclusion is expected to be gone.

skip_remediation_overdue.what: A validation exclusion is past the remediation date it declared.
skip_remediation_overdue.fix: Remediate the subtree, or renegotiate the date deliberately.

skip_subtree_contains_interactives.what: An excluded subtree contains operable widgets, so the page is hiding agent-operable surface behind the exclusion.
skip_subtree_contains_interactives.fix: Narrow the exclusion to the part that genuinely cannot be annotated.

strict_validation.what: Thrown, not reported: strict validation is on and register-time findings were raised, so the registration was refused.
strict_validation.fix: Fix the findings carried on the error, or register with strict validation off while migrating.

backend_unknown.what: Thrown, not reported: an action named a backend vocabulary term the runtime does not know.
backend_unknown.fix: Use a term from the backend vocabulary published in the spec, or register the extension that defines it.

invalid.what: Thrown, not reported: an argument failed validation at the API boundary.
invalid.fix: Read the message on the error; it names the argument and what it expected.

nac_id_duplicate_across_plugins.what: Two or more registered manifests declare the same nac_id, so an agent addressing it by id cannot know which element it gets.
nac_id_duplicate_across_plugins.fix: Namespace the ids with the plugin slug (plugin.element), or remove the declaration from the manifest that should not own it.

nac_id_orphan_in_dom.what: An element in the DOM carries a data-nac-id that no registered manifest declares, so it is reachable by name but not discoverable by an agent that reads the manifest.
nac_id_orphan_in_dom.fix: Declare it in the manifest, or drop the attribute if the element is not meant to be agent-addressable. Common and sometimes legitimate mid-migration, which is why it is a warning.

nac_id_declared_not_mounted.what: A manifest declares an id that is not currently in the DOM.
nac_id_declared_not_mounted.fix: Nothing, if the view is simply closed. If the manifest claims a permanent surface, mount it or stop declaring it.

nac_id_missing_plugin_prefix.what: A declared nac_id does not start with its plugin slug followed by a dot, so it loses the namespacing that keeps two plugins from colliding.
nac_id_missing_plugin_prefix.fix: Rename the id to slug.element. Renaming an id breaks every caller that used the old one, so do it with the same care as changing a URL.

duplicates.what: The same nac_id is declared by two or more registered plugins, so an agent addressing it by id cannot know which element it gets.

orphans.what: An element in the DOM carries a data-nac-id that no registered manifest declares. Common and sometimes legitimate during brownfield migration, which is why it is a warning.

unmounted.what: A manifest declares an id that is not currently in the DOM. Expected while a view is closed; a defect when the manifest claims a permanent surface.

convention_violations.what: A declared nac_id does not start with its plugin slug, so it loses the namespacing that keeps two plugins from colliding.

plugin_instance_violations.what: Plugin slug uniqueness is broken: the same slug is mounted more than once without distinct instance ids. Reported in its own bucket so CI can gate on it separately.

It can report unannotated interactive elements as candidates; whether each one belongs in the contract is the author's call. Any validator that reports this requirement as passed is overreaching.
